text: I know that isolating a single goal conceded can make it seem like I'm focusing too narrowly on one moment, but I think there were clear issues with City's defensive line on the first goal. The left-back should have positioned herself more centrally to avoid getting caught in behind, and the centre-back stepping across shouldn't have allowed the ball to be played into the penalty area so easily. Then, the cover behind that centre-back didn't arrive in time, which allowed the shot. On top of that, there was an unmarked player free at the far post beyond the shooter, meaning the right-back also failed to tuck in quickly enough. It feels like the team is overly focused on winning individual 1v1 duels and winning the ball back, at the expense of actually protecting the goal. This isn't a new issue—it was already visible even in the games they won by scoring multiple goals. Considering they conceded three goals in this match, I think the team really needs to rethink their defensive approach.
